## Multi-angle surfaces in Windows 0.24.26

When the local enhanced image model draws the initial reference, 3D Studio automatically renders the reconstructed mesh from the left, back and right. A single local image-to-image model refines those three guides in sequence. Workbench blends their material details onto the visible surfaces using the known camera positions, depth and surface normals. The original front photograph stays on its original facets. The resulting GLB carries the appearance around the sculpture when it rotates or opens in another viewer.

This adds texture detail. The shape still comes from a single reference, so an unseen contour or part can be inaccurate. Workspaces that use the smaller LCM image renderer retain the single-reference workflow. Complex meshes can store the additional generated colors per vertex to meet the 8 MiB export limit. The angle images and depth maps are temporary.

## Multi-angle surfaces, Windows 0.24.26

Rendered the same walnut red-panda mesh before and after at quarter turns. Verified its 107,136 oriented triangles, original front photo and front UVs were unchanged. The exported sample has four embedded textures. The new left, rear and right materials cover 17,293, 28,248 and 19,006 triangles respectively. All three synthesized images were conditioned on views of the actual mesh.

The packaged app created a new ceramic owl in 51.4 seconds on the RTX 3060, measured from clicking Create through retrieval of the saved preview. It has 82,100 triangles and four embedded textures. The previous single-view owl trial took 28.9 seconds with a different seed. The visible result depends on the prompt and the generated reference image. The saved preview and exported GLB matched byte for byte. Replaying the request returned the saved model and navigation during generation reconnected to its progress.
